content.user_title: Improve Dart Code with Static Analysis
content.value_statement: Dart diagnostics can be difficult to review and resolve before a commit. This skill guides Claude Code, Claude, and Codex through analysis, reviewed fixes, and formatting.
actual_capabilities: Guides execution of dart analyze for a selected Dart project or directory.
Describes targeted diagnostic suppression for generated code and false positives.
Uses dart fix --dry-run to preview supported mechanical changes.
Guides reviewed use of dart fix --apply and dart format.
Suggests rerunning analysis after fixes are applied.
limitations: It does not replace human review of diagnostics or automated changes.
It only addresses diagnostics supported by the installed Dart SDK and project packages.
It cannot determine whether a lint rule matches every project architecture.
Applying fixes can modify files, so users should review dry-run output first.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Flutter change for review
use_cases.description: Run analysis, inspect diagnostics, and format a Flutter change before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Configure stricter Dart diagnostics
use_cases.description: Set up analysis_options.yaml with recommended rules and strict type checks for a Dart package.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Dart codebase
use_cases.description: Preview and review supported automated fixes during a Dart SDK or API migration.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Dart static analysis for this project. Summarize each diagnostic and suggest the safest next step.

prompt_templates.title: Fix reported lints
prompt_templates.prompt: Run dart analyze, group the diagnostics by cause, and show which fixes are mechanical before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Preview automated fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run dart fix --dry-run for this package. Explain the proposed changes and wait for my approval before applying them.

prompt_templates.title: Harden analyzer settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review analysis_options.yaml and propose strict type checks and lint rules. Explain each change and preserve existing project-specific rules.

output_examples.input: Analyze this Flutter package before I commit.
output: Analysis completed with diagnostics grouped by error, warning, and info level.
Recommended fixes identify affected files and explain which changes require manual review.
A final verification step reruns analysis after approved changes.

output_examples.input: Preview automated Dart fixes without changing files.
output: Dry-run results list the proposed mechanical fixes.
The response highlights changes that may affect APIs or formatting.
No files are changed until the user approves applying fixes.

best_practices: Run dart analyze before committing or submitting a review.
Use dart fix --dry-run and review the proposed changes before applying them.
Keep analysis_options.yaml under version control with project-specific rules documented.
anti_patterns: Do not apply automated fixes without reviewing the dry-run output.
Do not suppress diagnostics broadly when a targeted fix is practical.
Do not treat a clean analysis run as a substitute for tests and code review.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It guides use of dart analyze, dart fix, and dart format for Dart and Flutter projects.

faq.question: Will it change my files automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends a dry run first. Applying fixes changes files only when the requested command is approved and run.

faq.question: Can it configure Flutter lint rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to configure analysis_options.yaml, including flutter_lints and strict analyzer settings.

faq.question: Can I use it with a pure Dart package?
faq.answer: Yes. The analysis and fix workflow applies to Dart packages, not only Flutter applications.

faq.question: Does it fix every diagnostic?
faq.answer: No. dart fix only supports certain mechanical changes. Other diagnostics need manual investigation and edits.

faq.question: Does a clean analysis replace testing?
faq.answer: No. Static analysis complements unit tests, integration tests, and human code review.
